title: Evidence‑led recovery offer — customer snapshot (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a draft customer‑facing snapshot and recovery offer for tenants impacted by the inference degradation on 2026‑10‑12 UTC. The doc is intentionally concise and evidence‑forward: we want customers to be able to validate impact for themselves and choose a recovery path (manual replay, opt‑in replay by Redwood, or decline).

Audience:
- Primary: engineering/product leads at affected customers
- Secondary: customer success managers and partner SREs who will send/maintain evidence bundles

Key messages (single paragraph for status page):
On 2026‑10‑12 at ~02:15–03:40 UTC we observed a regional inference degradation affecting a subset of streaming and short‑sequence generation requests in eu‑west and us‑central. The service remained available, but some requests returned truncated or stale structured outputs. We diagnosed a cache‑eviction race interacting with a new batching heuristic; fixes were deployed by 05:10 UTC and normal routing resumed. We are offering affected customers an evidence package and three recovery choices (self‑verify, opt‑in replay, or decline).

Concise timeline (operator times UTC):
- 02:12 — First customer reports (CS tickets JIRA‑INC‑4821, JIRA‑INC‑4824).
- 02:15 — Alerts triggered: increased structured output truncation and KV‑cache eviction warnings (SLOs: per‑token latency spike recorded).
- 02:40 — Pattern identified: degradation correlates with short‑sequence continuous‑batching windows + cache eviction bursts on instances with new batching flags (rollout cohort B).
- 03:05 — Rollback of batching heuristic to prior safe profile started for cohort B.
- 04:45 — Full rollback completes across impacted pools.
- 05:10 — Normal routing and baseline metrics restored; post‑deploy checks green.
- 06:00 — Evidence bundle generation completed for affected tenants.

What happened (plain language for customers):
A runtime change to an inference batching optimizer increased how aggressively requests were grouped. Under certain traffic patterns this triggered premature eviction of KV cache entries for ongoing streaming or short prompt sessions. The result: some responses lost recent context or were truncated when we serialized structured output. The change only affected a small cohort (internal rollout flag cohort B) and only particular hardware pools; the majority of traffic was unaffected.

Scope and impact (per‑tenant summary approach):
We have prepared per‑tenant evidence bundles that include: request timestamps (UTC), request ids, sample responses before/after, and operator trace ids to validate whether any given request was affected. These bundles do not include customer PII or payloads beyond the minimal fields needed for verification (we've redacted freeform user content by default).

Customer choices (we will include a compact form link in the status update):
1) Self‑verify (no action from Redwood): we provide the evidence bundle and instructions for how to run the verification checklist locally. Recommended for customers that want full control and have replay tooling.
2) Opt‑in replay by Redwood (recommended for customers who want a one‑time automated attempt): with consent we will attempt to reprocess affected requests through a stabilized pipeline and deliver best‑effort regenerated outputs. Expected window to complete: 48–72 hours after opt‑in confirmation depending on request volume. We will not retry requests where customer content was redacted or unavailable.
3) Decline — no replay, retain evidence only.

Verification checklist (for self‑verify):
- Download per‑tenant evidence bundle link (URL provided in email).
- Confirm request ids and timestamps against your app logs.
- Run simple heuristic: compare 'final_token_count' and 'sequence_hash' fields; mismatches likely indicate truncation.
- If you identify affected requests, collect an example payload (redacted if necessary) and provide CS with request id + example for replay or manual review.

Customer impact examples (non‑exhaustive):
- A chat session with rapid streaming could show one or two missing tokens at the end of a message (visible as truncated JSON field).
- Ranker outputs: rare cases where top‑k reranking returned stale scores because KV state referenced an earlier step.

Operational mitigations completed during incident:
- Immediate rollback of batching heuristic for rollout cohort B.
- Halt of further rollout until additional validation added.
- Regeneration job templates implemented to enable safe idempotent replay (sandboxed, rate‑limited).
- Extra telemetry added to KV cache evictions so we can alert earlier if pattern recurs.

Planned fixes and timeline (customer‑facing summary):
Short term (next 2 weeks): revert rollout flags, add pre‑flight checks to flag aggressive batching on low‑latency pools, and complete a gated canary with enhanced eviction telemetry.
Medium term (1–3 months): introduce stronger per‑session KV pinning for streaming sessions and a non‑disruptive cache warming mechanism.
Long term (3–6 months): model of safer continuous batching heuristics with guardrails for structured outputs; formal QA scenarios added to regression suite.

Data and privacy note:
- Evidence bundles redact freeform user content by default.
- If a customer chooses opt‑in replay and the original payload is required, we will ask for explicit consent to use full payloads and will follow the customer's data retention/handling rules.

Compensation and credits:
We are offering a one‑time service credit for tenants that choose opt‑in automated replay and can demonstrate business impact from the affected requests. Credit details and eligibility will be discussed via the account team; credits do not apply to requests where customer declines replay.

Customer communication templates (short forms to send):
- Status page blurb (50–120 chars): "Partial degradation in eu‑west/us‑central affecting structured outputs; fixes deployed and evidence‑led recovery choices available."
- Email subject line: "Redwood — Evidence package + replay options after 2026‑10‑12 inference degradation"
- Short CS note to attach evidence bundle: "Attached: per‑tenant verification bundle and a 3‑option recovery form. Reply with the option you'd like and any request ids to prioritize."

Open questions / items for the internal team (notes for CS + SRE coordination):
- Confirm exact credit amount threshold (billing/finance input needed). 
- Finalize opt‑in form flow and required legal consent language (legal review).
- Decide retention window for evidence bundles (suggest 30 days by default).
- Who signs off on the replay waveform limits (rate limits, safety checks)? Ops and security to confirm.

Owner and escalation:
- Customer Success owner: Maya Patel (maya@redwood.ai)
- Oncall SRE lead: Diego Martinez (#sre‑oncall slack)
- Product/Runtime contact: Hannah Kim

Draft email to customers (short):
Hi <CustomerName>,

On 2026‑10‑12 we detected a regional inference degradation that may have impacted some of your requests. We have prepared an evidence bundle you can use to verify impact and three recovery choices: self‑verify, opt‑in replay by Redwood, or decline. Please review the attached bundle and click the opt‑in link if you would like Redwood to attempt automated replay. If you’d prefer to handle verification yourself, follow the included checklist and reply with any request ids you want prioritized.

We apologize for the disruption and are committed to making it right — we’ll work with you on replay, credits, or manual remediation as needed.

— Maya (Customer Success)

Notes for publishing to status page: keep concise, link to a short FAQ + opt‑in form, and include expected time to complete replays (48–72 hrs) for customers who opt in.

Attachments to produce before publishing (checklist for CS ops):
- Per‑tenant evidence bundles (redacted) and hosted link.
- Short FAQ page: 4 Qs (what happened?, what will you do?, will my data be replayed?, how to opt out?).
- Opt‑in confirmation flow (small web form + consent checkbox).
- Internal incident postmortem (long form) linked for customers who request more detail.

Draft status page metadata (for internal use):
- severity: partial_degradation
- regions: eu‑west, us‑central
- affected_surface: structured_outputs, streaming_sessions (subset)
- start_time: 2026‑10‑12T02:15:00Z
- end_time: 2026‑10‑12T05:10:00Z

Publishing note: keep postmortem public‑friendly; avoid internal timelines that expose in‑progress blamable steps. Provide evidence and choices; customers who need deeper audit will be offered the longer postmortem under NDA if needed.

Revision history:
- 2026‑10‑14 draft created (Maya)
- 2026‑10‑15 added opt‑in replay mechanics (Diego)
- 2026‑10‑18 redaction rules clarified (Hannah)
- 2026‑10‑20 final internal review comments appended (Asha)

End of draft.
